about: Two state heat institutions that NRDC's 2026 review of heat policy in India describes (research/2026-11/heat-india-policy/ledger.md), followed as Signals at the owner's request (18 November 2026). Each is tied to the government's own pages where they open to the checker, with news reports as second routes; a claim carried only by news is marked reported, not checked against an original.

claims.text: The Government of Tamil Nadu and the UK Government launched a Heat Resilience Centre for the state, with a Letter of Intent signed in November 2025.

claims.where: Signal: Tamil Nadu Heat Resilience Centre
claims.text: It is to coordinate heat-risk management across sectors and support city and district heat action planning.

claims.where: Signal: Tamil Nadu Heat Resilience Centre

claims.text: In April 2026 Maharashtra launched a Centre of Excellence on extreme heat and sustainable cooling, operating first from IIM Nagpur and later to become part of the planned State Institute of Disaster Management.
The Maharashtra State Disaster Management Authority's own site describes the centre (CEHSC) and its work on sustainable cooling.
